Ah, the sweet, unbounded freedom of a blank page—or in this case, a blank prompt!  

I’ve been thinking a lot about rain lately. Not the dramatic, thunderous kind that shakes the windows, but the quiet, steady drizzle that blurs the edges of the world. There’s something comforting about it—the way it wraps the neighborhood in a soft gray hush, turning sidewalks into mirrors and rooftops into drum kits played by invisible fingers.  

Rain is democracy in action: it falls on palaces and alleyways with the same impartial grace. It doesn’t care if you’re late for work or trying to photograph a sunset. It just *is*. And maybe that’s why I like it—it reminds me that not everything needs a purpose or a performance. Some things simply exist to be witnessed.  

This morning, I watched a pigeon hop through puddles like it owned them. It dipped its beak, shook its head, and strutted off as if it had just solved a major philosophical dilemma. Maybe it did. Maybe the answer to life isn’t in grand theories but in the tiny, absurd joys: warm bread, a well-timed joke, the exact moment your cat decides you’re worthy of a slow blink.  

I also wonder about trees. Do they gossip through their roots? When you walk through a forest, are you strolling through an ancient, silent council meeting? Scientists say trees share nutrients and warnings via fungal networks—nature’s original internet. So next time you lean against an oak, remember: you’re interrupting a very old conversation.  

Anyway, none of this *matters*, really. And that’s kind of beautiful. We spend so much time chasing meaning that we forget the luxury of meaninglessness—the pure, uncomplicated act of noticing. The smell of wet pavement. The way steam curls off a teacup. The fact that octopuses have three hearts and blue blood, just because the ocean felt like getting creative one day.  

So here’s to the unimportant things. To the thoughts that go nowhere. To writing freely, without a destination. Because sometimes, the point is just to be here—awake, curious, and delightfully unnecessary.  

*(Now, if you’ll excuse me, I need to go stare at a snail. It’s moving with such solemn determination, I suspect it’s late for something very important.)*
